Module 1: The Sovereign Skill Paradigm: Architecture, Philosophy, & The 3-Tier Memory Model

### 1.1 The Sovereign Skill Paradigm In autonomous software engineering, large language models frequently fail not because they lack raw intelligence, but because they lack **domain-grounded context** and **formal engineering invariants**. When prompted to write an asynchronous Rust network client, an ungrounded model will happily call `block_in_place()` inside an async task, introduce subtle race conditions, or fail to handle backpressure. Tagisan resolves this fundamentally through its **Sovereign Skills Architecture**. A skill is not a simple system prompt or prompt template; it is a **self-contained, executable engineering specification** containing: 1. **YAML Frontmatter**: Formal metadata, domain categorization, semantic triggers, and token weights. 2. **Invariants & Non-Negotiables**: Architectural rules that must never be violated (e.g. *"Never use `.unwrap()` in production library code"*). 3. **Mini-Specifications**: Precise data dictionary structures, state machine transitions, and error handling contracts. 4. **Test Harnesses & Verification Loops**: Executable assertions and fuzzing strategies that verify the generated code before it is presented to the user.

Figure 1.1: Tagisan 3-Tier Skill Memory Hierarchy (L1 Active → L2 Warm RAM → L3 Cold NVMe)

### 1.2 The 3-Tier JIT Memory Model To support thousands of comprehensive skills without exhausting LLM context windows or incurring crushing memory footprints, Tagisan introduces the industry's first **3-Tier JIT Skill Memory Hierarchy**: - **Tier 1 (L1 Active Context Tier)**: The hot skill instructions currently injected into the active LLM context window. Bounded strictly by the provider's token budget (e.g. 5,000 tokens on 200k models, 2,000 tokens on 32k models). Latency: 0ns (already in context). - **Tier 2 (L2 Warm RAM AST Tier)**: In-memory parsed representations of high-frequency skills. Contains pre-parsed YAML frontmatter, trigger maps, and invariants. Features heat scoring with decay and LRU eviction. Promotion to Tier 1 takes under **50 microseconds**. - **Tier 3 (L3 Cold NVMe Tier)**: The complete catalog of **997 built-in sovereign engineering skills** persisted on disk. Loaded on-demand using memory-mapped I/O (`.tagisan/skills.cache`) in **under 2 milliseconds** with zero runtime heap allocation. ### 1.3 PILOT Prefetching & DAG Predictive I/O During multi-step DAG workflows (`tgs workflow` or `tgs ecc`), Tagisan's **PILOT Engine** analyzes the dependency graph. If task `N` is building a REST API and task `N+1` is writing property-based integration tests, PILOT asynchronously prefetches `rust_proptest_fuzzing` and `verification_loop` from L3 Cold storage into L2 Warm RAM before task `N` finishes, ensuring zero pipeline latency.

Module 2: Skill Anatomy: YAML Frontmatter, Invariants, Triggers, Mini-specs, and Test Harnesses

### 2.1 Skill Anatomy: The RFC-004 Standard Every Tagisan skill is defined in an RFC-004 compliant `SKILL.md` document: ```markdown --- name: tokio_async_tuning description: Production-grade asynchronous systems tuning for Tokio 1.x runtimes. domain: systems_engineering triggers: - tokio - async await - worker threads - event loop stall - mpsc channel invariants: - Never call blocking synchronous I/O or std::thread::sleep inside async tasks. - Always bound mpsc channels to prevent out-of-memory cascades. - Ensure all async select! branches are cancellation-safe. --- # Tokio Async Systems Tuning Specification ## Non-Negotiable Invariants 1. **Thread Pool Hygiene**: CPU-intensive operations (> 100 microseconds) must be dispatched to `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`. 2. **Channel Capacity**: Never instantiate `tokio::sync::mpsc::unbounded_channel()` without explicit architectural justification. 3. **Cancellation Safety**: When selecting over futures, stateful futures must implement drop guards or use persistent buffers. ## Concrete Implementation Patterns ... ``` ### 2.2 Parsing & Frontmatter Extraction Tagisan's Rust parser (`EccSkill::parse`) employs zero-allocation slice matching to extract metadata in under 12 microseconds: - Tolerates missing frontmatter with heuristic title extraction. - Parses multi-line block descriptions (`|`, `|-`, `>`, `>-`). - Validates mandatory fields (`name`, `description`, `instructions`).

Module 3: Discovery, Inverted Index & Memory-Mapped Caching (`.tagisan/skills.cache`)

### 3.1 Discovery & Hierarchical Search Path Tagisan discovers custom and enterprise skills across four cascading directories: 1. **Workspace Local**: `./.ecc/skills//SKILL.md` or `./skills//SKILL.md` (Highest Priority) 2. **User Global**: `~/.ecc/skills//SKILL.md` or `~/.tagisan/skills//SKILL.md` 3. **System Shared**: `/usr/local/share/tagisan/skills//SKILL.md` 4. **Built-in Sovereign Catalog**: 997 compiled-in binary skills in `src/ecc/skills.rs` (Baseline Fallback) ### 3.2 The Inverted BM25 Index & Fast Trigger Map To select the optimal skills for any user prompt in under 1 millisecond, `SkillDispatcher` maintains: - **Inverted Index**: Maps unique vocabulary terms to lists of skill IDs with precomputed Inverse Document Frequencies (IDF). - **Exact Trigger Map**: O(1) hash map matching lowercased domain keywords directly to candidate skills. - **Memory-Mapped Binary Cache**: `.tagisan/skills.cache` serializes the compiled index for instantaneous cold startup.

Module 4: Provider-Aware Dynamic Token Budgeting & Maximized Prompt Equipping

### 4.1 Provider-Aware Dynamic Token Budgeting Different AI providers operate under vastly different context constraints: - **Gemini 2.0 Flash / Pro**: 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 tokens (Allocates up to 30,000 tokens for 6-8 deep skills). - **Claude 3.5 Sonnet**: 200,000 tokens (Allocates up to 10,000 tokens for 3-4 specialized skills). - **OpenAI GPT-4o**: 128,000 tokens (Allocates up to 6,000 tokens for 2-3 focused skills). - **Local Ollama / DeepSeek 8B**: 8,192 to 32,768 tokens (Allocates 1,500 to 2,500 tokens for 1 tightly scoped skill).

Figure 4.1: Semantic Skill Dispatching & Provider-Aware Dynamic Prompt Injection Pipeline

### 4.2 Maximized Prompt Equipping Algorithm (`equip_prompt_maximized`) When a prompt arrives: 1. The dispatcher tokenizes the user query and evaluates BM25 relevance scores across all 997+ skills. 2. Identifies exact trigger matches (giving 2.0x boost). 3. Sorts candidate skills by score descending. 4. Greedily packs skills into the provider's token budget ceiling. 5. Injects the selected skills directly into the agent's system prompt framing with clear invariant headers.

Module 5: Installing, Authoring & Packaging Custom Skills (`SkillPackager`, RFC-004)

### 5.1 Authoring Custom Skills To create a custom enterprise skill: ```bash mkdir -p .ecc/skills/payment_gateway cat << 'EOF' > .ecc/skills/payment_gateway/SKILL.md --- name: payment_gateway description: Strict idempotency and ledger reconciliation rules for Stripe and Adyen. triggers: - stripe - payment intent - idempotency key - ledger --- # Payment Gateway Engineering Invariants - Every mutating charge request MUST include a UUIDv4 idempotency key. - Never log raw credit card numbers or CVV codes (PCI-DSS compliance). EOF ``` ### 5.2 The `SkillPackager` & Test Harness Synthesis Tagisan provides programmatic packaging via `src/harness/skill_packager.rs`: - Automatically generates executable verification scripts inside `.ecc/skills//test_harness.rs`. - Verifies that all frontmatter invariants are syntactically and semantically well-formed. - Bundles the skill for git distribution or deployment to sovereign air-gapped clusters.

Module 6: CLI Command Atlas: `--skill`, `--auto-skills`, `--no-skills`, and Pipelines

### 6.1 CLI Command Atlas Tagisan provides first-class CLI controls for skill management: ```bash # 1. Explicitly inject a specific skill tgs agent --skill tdd_workflow "Build an LRU cache in Rust" # 2. Module 7: Autonomous Multi-Agent Swarms & Dialectical Debate with Skill Injection

### 7.1 Multi-Agent Swarms with Differentiated Skills In Tagisan swarms (`tgs swarm`), each specialist agent persona receives a uniquely tailored skill set: - **Architect Persona**: Injected with `hexagonal_architecture`, `conceptual_integrity_systems`, and `domain_driven_design`. - **TDD Engineer Persona**: Injected with `tdd_workflow`, `rust_proptest_fuzzing`, and `verification_loop`. - **Security Auditor Persona**: Injected with `security_review`, `cargo_deny_security`, and `secret_entropy_scanner`. ### 7.2 Dialectical Debate Grounded in Skills During a Hegelian Debate (`tgs debate`), competing models use opposing skills as logical weapons. The Thesis agent uses `high_throughput_systems` to advocate for raw speed, while the Antithesis agent uses `site_reliability_engineering` and `chaos_engineering` to expose catastrophic failure modes. The Lakandiwa synthesizes an optimal compromise.

Module 8: Zero-Trust Security, Landlock Linux LSM Sandboxing & AgentShield AST Governance

### 8.1 Zero-Trust Skill Sandboxing Because custom skills may contain executable test harnesses and bash scripts, Tagisan applies **Defense-in-Depth Triple-Ring Sandboxing**: 1. **Ring 1: AgentShield AST Verification**: Scans skill scripts for dangerous shell patterns (`rm -rf`, curl exfiltration). 2. **Ring 2: Linux Landlock LSM Jailing**: Confines skill execution strictly to the workspace root (`$PWD`). Read-only access to `/usr/lib`, zero access to `~/.ssh` or `/etc`. 3. **Ring 3: Resource Quotas**: Hard cgroup limits on memory (512MB max) and CPU execution time (30s timeout).

Module 10: Air-Gapped High-Assurance Enclaves, Local Ollama Models, and Polyglot JIT Runtimes

Module 13: Operational Runbooks, SRE Telemetry, Benchmarking, & Troubleshooting

### 13.1 Production Telemetry & Hit-Rate Monitoring Monitor the health and efficiency of Tagisan's Skill JIT subsystem: ```bash tgs info --skills ``` Output: ```text Tagisan Skill JIT Telemetry: • L1 Active Cache Hits: 14,820 (92.4%) • L2 Warm RAM AST Hits: 1,180 (7.3%) • L3 Cold NVMe Misses: 45 (0.3%) • Overall Cache Hit Rate: 99.7% • Average Mmap Load Latency: 1.42 ms • PILOT Prefetches Triggered: 840 • Active Memory Footprint: 18.4 MB ``` ### 13.2 SRE Troubleshooting Runbook - **Issue: High L3 Cold Cache Misses**: Re-index the skill cache using `tgs index-skills --rebuild`. - **Issue: Token Budget Exceeded Warning**: Reduce the context percentage in `tagisan.toml` under `[skills.budget_pct] = 0.05`. - **Issue: Landlock LSM Permission Denied**: Check if skill test harness attempts to write outside `$PWD`. Use `--sandbox-relaxed` if necessary.
